# ToggleGroup

> A row of Toggles where one is chosen, like a year switcher. Arrow keys move the choice, and the row is one stop for Tab.

| `toggles` | slot |  |  |

## Anatomy

- `root`: The `role="radiogroup"`. No surface of its own: the toggles sit side by side.

## When to use

- **One of a few, straight away.** Picking one of a few options that all fit on a line, where the choice applies straight away: a year, a view, a period.

## When not to use

- **Too many options.** More options than fit on one line. That's a menu.
- **Switching panels.** Switching panels of content under it. That's **Tabs**.
- **Several on at once.** Several things that can be on at once. Those are Toggles on their own, each `aria-pressed`.

## Behaviour

One toggle is on at a time. Choosing another turns the last one off. The group draws nothing itself; each Toggle shows its own on and off.

In Figma it has a page of its own: a component with a `toggles` slot of Toggle instances. Figma's Toggle has no label yet, so the Figma group shows three icon toggles, not years.

## Accessibility

- **Element**: `role="radiogroup"` holding Toggles with `role="radio"` and `aria-checked`. Toggle sets `aria-checked` itself when it has `role="radio"`.
- **Name**: `label` becomes the group's `aria-label`. A Toggle with only an icon still needs its own `aria-label`.
- **Keyboard**: Tab lands on the chosen toggle, and the next Tab leaves the group. Arrow keys move to the next or previous toggle and choose it, Home and End go to the first and last, as the ARIA radio group pattern has it. Disabled toggles are skipped.
- **Focus**: Each Toggle's own focus ring, on `:focus-visible`.

## Content

Short labels of about the same length, so the row reads as one set.
